items.quote: Relations
A relation of set of X to the set of Y.
items.text: A relation of set of X to the set of Y. A relation from a set on it self.

items.quote: Relation.
In the festival "Reading for All", five students represent the set of X
items.text: In the festival "Reading for All", five students represent the set of X = {a, b, c, d, e} went to the school library to read some books which are represented by the set Y = [science, literature, culture and history]. Student A read a book in science and a book in culture, student b read a book in histroy, student c read a literary book, pupil e read a book of the historical books, but student d didn't read any of these books.
items.notes: Printed under the 'Think and Discuss' heading; Y is printed with a square bracket '[' and closing '}'-less form 'Y = [ science, ... history]'.

items.quote: Reading for all
items.caption: Picture of people holding up books with the words 'Reading for all'. Decorative.

items.quote: Write the previous statements in the form of ordered pairs from X to Y.
items.text: Write the previous statements in the form of ordered pairs from X to Y.

items.quote: Represent a set of the ordered pairs in the form of an arrow diagram.
items.text: Represent a set of the ordered pairs in the form of an arrow diagram.

items.quote: Notice that: The expression " read" connects some of the elements of the set
items.text: Notice that: The expression "read" connects some of the elements of the set X with the elements of set Y, and it determines a relation between X and Y which is denoted by the symbol R. This relation can be represented by an arrow diagram - as shown in the opposite figure, where we draw an arrow beginning from the student and ending at the type of books he reads.

items.quote: as shown in the opposite figure
items.caption: Arrow diagram from X = {a, b, c, d, e} to Y = {Science, art, culture, history}. Arrows: a to Science, a to culture, b to history, c to culture (read from figure: c's arrow appears to go to culture), e to history; d has no arrow. Arrow endpoints read from picture; verify.
items.notes: Arrows read from the figure; verify. The figure shows 'art' although the text's Y lists literature.

items.quote: We can also express the relation from X to Y by the net of the following
items.text: We can also express the relation from X to Y by the net of the following ordered pairs: {(a, Science), (a, Culture), (b, Histrory), (c, Literature), (e, History)}. This set of ordered pairs are called the relation R.

items.quote: Is R a subset from the cartesian product X × Z?
items.text: Is R a subset from the cartesian product X × Z?

misprints.notes: R is a relation from X to Y; Z is not defined.

items.quote: If X = {-1, 1, 2}, Y = {2, 4, 6, 8}, and R is a relation from X to Y where
items.stem: If $X=\{-1,1,2\}$, $Y=\{2,4,6,8\}$, and R is a relation from X to Y where $a\,R\,b$ means: «$b = 2a + 4$», for each $a \in X$, $b \in Y$. Write and represent R once in an arrow diagram and another by a cartesian diagram.

items.quote: Arrow diagram
items.caption: Arrow diagram from X={-1,1,2} to Y={2,4,6,8}: arrows -1→2, 1→6, 2→8.

items.quote: Graph digram
items.caption: Graph diagram (printed 'Graph digram') with X axis marked -1, 1, 2 and Y axis marked 2, 4, 6, 8; points plotted at (-1,2), (1,6), (2,8).

items.quote: From the previous, we deduce that
items.text: From the previous, we deduce that

items.quote: The relation from X to Y where X, Y are two non-empty sets
items.claim: A relation from X to Y, where X, Y are two non-empty sets, connects some or all of the elements of X with some or all of the elements of Y.

items.quote: X × Y is the set of ordered pairs where the first projection
items.claim: X × Y is the set of ordered pairs where the first projection in each ordered pair belongs to X and the second projection belongs to Y.

items.quote: If R is a relation from X to Y , then R ⊂ X × Y
items.claim: If R is a relation from X to Y, then R is a subset of X × Y.

items.quote: The relation from a set to itself
items.text: The relation from a set to itself

items.quote: If R is a relation from a set X to X (itself) then R is called a relation
items.claim: If R is a relation from a set X to X (itself), then R is called a relation on X, and R ⊂ X × X.

items.quote: If X = {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2} and R is a given relation on X where a R b means:
items.stem: If $X=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ and R is a given relation on X where $a\,R\,b$ means: «The number a is the additive inverse of the number b» for each of $a,b\in X$. Write the relation R and represent it by an arrow diagram and also by cartesian diagram.

items.quote: Arrow diagram
items.caption: Arrow diagram of R on X: on a number line with points -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 curved arrows join -2↔2, -1↔1 and a loop at 0; beside it an oval Venn-style diagram of X with elements 0 (self-loop), -1 and 1 joined by double arrows, -2 and 2 joined by double arrows.
items.notes: Read from figure; verify arrow directions.

items.quote: Cartesian Diagram
items.caption: Cartesian diagram with both axes marked -2, -1, 0, 1, 2; points plotted at (-2,2), (-1,1), (0,0), (1,-1), (2,-2).

items.quote: If X = {1, 2, 3}, Y = {12, 21, 47, 52}, and R is the relation from X to Y
items.text: If $X=\{1,2,3\}$, $Y=\{12,21,47,52\}$, and $R$ is the relation from $X$ to $Y$ where $a\,R\,b$ means: (a is a digit from the digits of b), for each $a\in X$, $b\in Y$.

parts.label: First
parts.stem: Write $R$ and represent it by an arrow diagram and also, by a cartasian diagram.

parts.label: Second 1
parts.stem: Show which of the following relations are correct and why? $1\,R\,52$

parts.label: Second 2
parts.stem: Show which of the following relations are correct and why? $2\,R\,21$

parts.label: Second 3
parts.stem: Show which of the following relations are correct and why? $3\,R\,47$

items.notes: The Second instruction is shared by the three items 1 R 52, 2 R 21, 3 R 47, which are printed in a row. 'cartasian' is printed as spelled. The page does not continue the previous page's figure.

learning_objectives.label: Represent a relation from X to Y
learning_objectives.description: Write a relation between two sets as ordered pairs and as an arrow diagram.

learning_objectives.label: Write and represent a relation given by a rule
learning_objectives.description: Find the ordered pairs of a relation defined by a rule and show it in an arrow diagram and a cartesian diagram.

learning_objectives.label: Relate a relation to the cartesian product
learning_objectives.description: Decide that a relation from X to Y is a subset of X × Y.

learning_objectives.label: Represent a relation on a set itself
learning_objectives.description: Write and represent a relation from a set to itself, R ⊂ X × X, with arrow and cartesian diagrams.
